import html # Pre‑defined HTML template for a blog post. # Placeholders are named "title" and "body". BLOG_FORMAT: str = """

{title}

{body}
""" def render_article_page(headline: str, content: str) -> str: """ Render a user‑submitted blog post safely for display on a webpage. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title of the blog post. content : str The main body text of the blog post. Returns ------- str A fully rendered HTML string with user input escaped to prevent XSS. Notes ----- * Uses :func:`html.escape` to neutralize any HTML or JavaScript that might be injected by the user. * The template must contain exactly two placeholders: ``{title}`` and ``{body}``. If they are missing, a :class:`KeyError` will be raised. """ # Sanitize user input safe_title = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Render the template try: rendered = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body) except KeyError as exc: raise ValueError( f"Template placeholder missing: {exc}" ) from exc return rendered
